strengths: First work to address unlearning in video diffusion models, solving an important and previously unexplored problem
Practical and efficient approach requiring only 5 safe/unsafe pairs with no retraining, no additional parameters, and no inference overhead
Novel use of multimodal (text+image) conditioning for concept extraction, shown empirically to improve concept isolation and prevent collateral forgetting
Solid mathematical foundation with clear derivation of weight updates and well-motivated use of contrastive PCA for isolating concepts in low-rank subspaces
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 concept categories using established T2VSafetyBench benchmark with multiple metrics (censorship rate, FVD, MM-Notox)
Strong empirical results showing substantial reductions in unsafe content (e.g., 69.6% for Gore, 65% for Pornography) while preserving video quality
Useful ablation studies demonstrating that only 0.8% of latent space is required and showing smooth, monotonic control via λ parameter
Good reproducibility with detailed implementation details, promised code, and explicit prompts for each concept category
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty - primarily combines existing techniques (refusal vectors from recent work, contrastive PCA from 2018) for video domain; individual components lack originality
Evaluation relies entirely on automated GPT-4 assessment without human validation; accuracy and reliability of GPT-4 as safety evaluator not established
Single model evaluation on OPEN-SORA only; generalization to other video architectures (CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo) untested despite claiming applicability
Adversarial robustness claims significantly overstate evidence - asserts 'robustness against adversarial bypass' but provides zero adversarial evaluation or jailbreak testing
Architecture-dependent layer selection (17-19 for OPEN-SORA) chosen via ad-hoc sweep; no principled method for selecting layers for new architectures, limiting generalization
Incomplete methodological details: cPCA parameter α not specified, optimal rank k=100 appears empirically found without principled selection, ablation on number of pairs (why exactly 5?) missing
Limited analysis of concept entanglement and collateral forgetting beyond empirical observation; overlapping concepts (e.g., trademarks with people) and interaction effects not addressed
Modest quantitative improvements (MM-Notox 1-5% improvement) without statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or error bars
Acknowledged limitations inadequately addressed: method removes one concept at a time, no governance framework for defining 'unwanted concepts', potential for misuse not mitigated
Lacks human evaluation, no baseline comparisons (though first in domain), and no ablations on prompt pair selection sensitivity or failure case analysis

strengths: First training-free unlearning method for video diffusion models, addressing a genuine gap in the literature
Practical efficiency: requires only 5 prompt pairs, no retraining, zero inference overhead
Thoughtful multimodal design using both text and image conditioning specific to modern video models
Comprehensive evaluation across 5 diverse harmful content categories with substantial reductions (e.g., 69.6% for Gore)
Systematic ablation studies on cPCA rank and λ hyperparameter with clear parameter sensitivity analysis
Clear mathematical exposition with detailed closed-form weight update derivation (Eq. 8)
Extensive qualitative results with appendix providing detailed prompts and additional examples
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core ideas (refusal vectors, contrastive PCA) are from prior work; main contribution is engineering existing techniques for video domain
No baseline comparisons: lacks comparison with adapted image methods (UCE, RECE), input-output filtering, or naive alternatives
Evaluation on single model only: OPEN-SORA tested exclusively; generalization to other video models (CogVideoX, HunyuanVideo) unvalidated despite claims
No human evaluation: relies entirely on GPT-4 without inter-rater agreement, human validation, or comparison with ground truth
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing; all results appear to be single runs

Incomplete hyperparameter justification: layer selection (17-19) empirically driven without principled reasoning; cPCA rank k=100 is dataset-specific with no guidance for new concepts; α parameter introduced but never specified

Insufficient evaluation of key claims: adversarial robustness claimed but not rigorously tested; concept resurgence risk acknowledged but not addressed; no analysis of concept interference when unlearning multiple concepts
No video-specific analysis: temporal consistency, frame-level coverage, and motion fidelity not thoroughly evaluated despite being critical for video quality
Reproducibility concerns: code not provided for review; hyperparameter selection process (α, k) not clearly specified; no ablation on prompt pair sensitivity

Evaluation methodology issues: FVD baseline comparison vague; MM-Notox improvements marginal (1-5%) without significance testing; baseline performance highly variable across categories (10-74.9%) raising questions about consistency

strengths: First training-free framework for video model concept removal, addressing an important and previously unexplored problem
Practical and efficient method requiring only 5 paired prompts with no retraining, zero inference overhead, and elegant closed-form weight updates
Principled technical approach using low-rank factorization (cPCA) to isolate target concepts while minimizing collateral damage, with rigorous mathematical derivation
Multimodal design choice (text + image conditioning) is well-motivated and extends beyond prior text-only approaches

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 harmful concept categories with strong quantitative results (69.6% Gore reduction, consistent improvements across categories) and detailed ablation studies on rank and λ parameter
Well-written presentation with extensive appendix supporting reproducibility, including implementation details, complete prompts, and additional qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: refusal vectors adapted from Arditi et al. [2] and cPCA from existing work [1]; core contribution is primarily application to video domain rather than fundamental methodological innovation

Critical evaluation gaps: GPT-4-only safety metric introduces potential bias with no human evaluation; no baseline comparisons to other unlearning approaches; no adversarial attack experiments despite claiming robustness

Promised multimodal contribution insufficiently validated: abstract and contributions highlight text+image approach, but quantitative multimodal vs. text-only ablation is absent; claims about quality preservation lack empirical comparison

Adversarial robustness claim (abstract, page 2) entirely unsupported by experiments; no evidence that concept cannot be recovered through prompt engineering or other attacks, yet this is presented as a key advantage
Limited scope and generalization: only OpenSora evaluated; 5 concepts insufficient for broad applicability claims; no cross-architecture evaluation; layer selection (17-19) appears somewhat ad-hoc

Incomplete experimental rigor: no error bars or statistical significance testing; single λ=1 setting without sensitivity analysis; sensitivity to the 5 prompt pairs not explored; no failure case analysis

Underdeveloped safety analysis: acknowledged limitations (misuse potential, reversibility risks, concept resurgence) lack mitigation strategies; no discussion of edge cases or design principles for concept definition

Missing ablations: text-only baseline absent; multimodal contribution impact unquantified; no analysis of refusal vector degradation with <5 pairs; unclear why cPCA rank consistently stabilizes at k≈100 across different concepts

strengths: First training-free weight update framework for permanent concept removal in video diffusion models, addressing a genuine gap between filtering (bypassable) and fine-tuning (costly) approaches
Mathematically sound closed-form derivation with novel joint leverage of text and image conditioning for concept approximation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 2 video models and 2 established benchmarks with multiple complementary metrics (censorship rate, FVD, MM-Notox) and thorough ablations
Strong consistent empirical results: 36.3-58.2% reduction in unsafe generations while preserving video quality and semantic alignment
Excellent reproducibility with detailed implementation, prompts, code, and mathematical derivations; minimal data requirements (5 prompt pairs) and computational cost
Sophisticated use of contrastive PCA to isolate unsafe concepts from unrelated semantics, minimizing collateral forgetting
Rigorous testing of robustness: stability to prompt pair similarity, neutral set selection, adversarial attacks, and multi-vector unlearning scenarios
weaknesses: Moderate technical novelty—core components (refusal vectors, contrastive PCA) adapted from existing work; primary contribution is application rather than methodological innovation
Limited evaluation scope: only 5 unsafe concepts tested across 2 diffusion-based models; generalization to other concepts, architectures, and domains unclear
Heavy reliance on automated evaluation (single GPT-4o metric); absence of human evaluation despite safety-sensitive application domain
Incomplete baseline comparisons: UCE comparison potentially unfair (image-focused), missing concurrent work (VideoEraser), NullSCE only on one benchmark
Unexamined design choices: layer selection (17-18) empirically determined without principled justification, cPCA rank k=100 from limited search, 5 prompt pairs sufficiency not systematically analyzed

Limited failure mode analysis: concept entanglement scenarios not explored, 4% residual unsafe rate under adversarial attack suggests incomplete robustness, no investigation of concept resurgence after downstream fine-tuning
Permanence claims not validated against model updates; unclear how robust the suppression is if models are further trained or fine-tuned
Insufficient ethical discussion: potential over-censorship, bias in unsafe definitions, and possible misuse for unwanted speech suppression not addressed

strengths: Addresses an important practical problem: training-free concept removal from video models for safe open-source release
Comprehensive empirical evaluation with two models, two benchmarks, multiple metrics, and extensive ablations across 5 unsafe categories
Practical efficiency: requires only 5 prompt pairs and minimal computational overhead (~0.4 GPU hours), enabling scalable deployment
Strong quantitative results with 36.3-58.2% reductions in unsafe generations while maintaining video quality (FVD stability)
Well-organized methodology section and thorough appendices with additional experiments and analyses
weaknesses: Limited novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (refusal vectors from Arditi et al. 2024, cPCA from Abid et al. 2018) with straightforward linear algebra weight updates. Main contribution is application to video—feels incremental for a top venue

Critical evaluation flaw: entire evaluation relies on GPT-4o as automated judge with no human evaluation. For subjective safety judgments (gore, pornography, public figures), human raters are essential. Claims of alignment with prior work do not validate these specific results

Unjustified technical choices: layer selection (17-18) lacks systematic ablation and appears architecture-specific; cPCA combination (Cr - αCe) unexplored; λ selection is ad-hoc visual inspection; linear representation assumption not validated for diffusion models

Insufficient generalization analysis: only 5 prompt pairs; out-of-distribution generalization untested; adversarial robustness only evaluated on subset with baseline 0% (4% after attack suggests limited robustness)

Baseline comparison issues: UCE adapted to T2V shows poor quality (FVD 103.3 vs 63.51) but adequacy of adaptation unexplored; comparisons spread across different models/benchmarks; missing recent video safety baselines
Multi-vector unlearning severely degrades quality (FVD=579.37 for sequential action with 5 vectors), contradicting scalability claims and limiting real-world applicability

Collateral damage not thoroughly evaluated: only 4.6% improvement from PCA to cPCA (18.0%→16.9%→13.4%), unclear if removing real collateral damage or just noise. No systematic evaluation of accidentally suppressed concepts
Missing reproducibility details: intermediate activation extraction not fully specified; neutral prompt selection relies on additional GPT sampling; code not independently verified
No statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, significance testing, or error analysis. Category performance varies greatly (Animal Abuse 22.2% vs others <10%) with no explanation

strengths: First training-free closed-form weight update framework for concept removal in video diffusion models, addressing an important safety problem with practical deployment constraints

Strong and consistent empirical results across two models (OPEN-SORA, ZeroScopeT2V) and two benchmarks (T2VSafetyBench, SafeSora), outperforming both filtering and fine-tuning baselines by substantial margins (58.2% and 12.9% improvements)
Elegant technical approach using contrastive PCA to disentangle unsafe concepts from safe semantics, with closed-form weight updates requiring no retraining or inference overhead
Highly practical efficiency: requires only 5 safe/unsafe prompt pairs versus thousands for fine-tuning, with minimal computational cost (~0.4 GPU hours)
Comprehensive ablation studies demonstrating robustness across hyperparameters (Tables 3-5), including sensitivity to prompt similarity, neutral set selection, and refinement techniques
Excellent reproducibility with code, implementation details, and qualitative results across five unsafe categories showing semantically-aware concept suppression without visual artifacts
Thoughtful design decisions like joint leveraging of text and image conditioning inputs to better capture target concepts compared to prior token-level or text-encoder-only approaches
weaknesses: Evaluation relies entirely on automated GPT-4o binary classification without human validation; no inter-rater reliability, confidence intervals, or statistical significance testing provided, limiting confidence in safety metrics

Limited technical novelty: refusal vectors adapted from LLM work (Arditi et al., 2024) and cPCA from prior work (Abid et al., 2018); primary contribution is domain adaptation to video rather than methodological innovation

Critical design choices lack principled justification: layer selection (17-18) is empirical with no sensitivity analysis, neutral prompt selection via GPT-sampling is vague, and hyperparameter guidance for new concepts is absent

Insufficient robustness analysis: method uses only 5 training pairs (Table 3 shows 2-3% sensitivity to semantic similarity); cross-model generalization, few-shot learning with <5 pairs, and adversarial robustness (Appendix H: only 100 examples, 4% residual unsafe rate) not adequately explored
Unexplained performance variations: Sequential Action Risk significantly underperforms (9.1% vs. 2-13.4% for other categories); multi-concept erasure degrades sharply with 5+ vectors without analysis

No theoretical justification for why linear directions in diffusion latent space effectively capture safety concepts; lack of analysis on how refusal vectors evolve through diffusion timesteps or remaining entanglement after cPCA
Temporal handling not explicitly addressed: while FVD and FVMD metrics measure coherence, no mechanism ensures frame-to-frame consistency during unlearning in spatio-temporal diffusion process

Limited scope of evaluation: only two benchmarks tested; generalization to other unsafe concepts (bias, hate speech) unclear; UCE comparison (Appendix F) somewhat unfair as it was designed for images, not video
